The 2-loop diagnostic collapsed to 493 (502/473/504; per-sample dev accuracy 0.27-0.31 against 0.40-0.46 at 8 loops), so metric minus diag is +136, but only because 2 loops stopped being trained: at 8 loops itself per-sample dev accuracy was 0.40-0.46 against 500's 0.48 on seed 0. The fixed depth did not help the depth it was trained at. RL at 8 loops found proofs fast: after one round of 12 attempts, seeds 0 and 1 had solved 677 and 637 targets (500: 287 after 32 attempts over 1/2/4/8); seed 2 started at 208 (round-1 variance, as in the spike) and reached 1054 by round 5. RL-target accuracy at 8 loops ended at 0.66-0.72 (500: 0.76) and final solved 1127/1047/1054 (500: 1198). A round cost 335-380 s (the fine-tune at 8 loops 160-215 s against about 110 s at random 1-8; sampling 160-190 s charged), so seed 1 got 4 rounds. Fewer attempts and rounds explain part of the loss, but not the lower per-sample accuracy at the trained depth: the random 1-8 draw in fine-tuning acts as a regularizer (stochastic depth), not as the suppressor of deep passes I hypothesized. Pretraining was unchanged and again depth-invariant (val loss within 0.002 across 1-8 loops on every seed). Next: keep random depths in the fine-tune and change something else (deep supervision, a loop-count signal, or more attempts at deep loops only). |
